source: AISC Design Guide 1, 2nd Edition — Base Plate and Anchor Rod Design
status: complete — this is the DESIGN BASIS itself, not a tool that implements it
why_this_outranks_the_profis_runs: PROFIS is one implementation of one method. DG 1 is the document the project's design basis names. A disagreement with PROFIS is a question; a disagreement with DG 1 would be a defect. That asymmetry is why four PROFIS runs could not settle what one reading of Sect. 3.4.1 did.

3.3.4.relation: q = f_p(max) * B, FULL plate width

the_key_line: DG 1's moment equation about point B is q_max*Y*(N/2 - Y/2 + f) - Pr*(e+f) = 0. The lever arm N/2 - Y/2 places the bearing resultant at the PLATE EDGE, over the FULL width B. That is exactly what the module does.

resolution_of_candidate_defect_9a.was: the module read 21-39% low against PROFIS's equivalent-rigid anchor forces across Cases C, D and E, and the bias grew with axial load. Three candidate replacement models were proposed and all three were rejected by further runs.
resolution_of_candidate_defect_9a.now: the module implements DG 1 Sect. 3.4.1 correctly. The gap is a genuine METHOD difference: DG 1 uses a uniform plastic bearing block over the whole plate at the compression edge; PROFIS's CBFEM concentrates bearing near the column footprint.
resolution_of_candidate_defect_9a.consequence: adopting PROFIS-like anchor tensions would be a change of DESIGN BASIS, not a bug fix. The gap stays recorded in profis_baseplate_cases.json so the choice is visible on any calculation sheet.
resolution_of_candidate_defect_9a.lesson: four PROFIS runs established that two tools differ but could never say which was right. Only the governing document could. Comparing an implementation against another implementation is not verification against a standard.

defect_13.title: DG 1 Eq. 3.3.15 (Y < l bearing-interface thickness) was missing entirely
defect_13.was: the module always used Eq. 3.3.14, tp = l*sqrt(2*fp/(phi*Fy))
defect_13.now: tp = sqrt(4*fp*Y*(l - Y/2)/(phi*Fy)) when Y < l
defect_13.direction: CONSERVATIVE — 3.3.15 <= 3.3.14 for all Y < l, and they meet at Y = l
defect_13.not_hypothetical: Case C has Y = 52.46 mm against m = 82.5 mm, so the branch applies

defect_14.title: tension-interface thickness halved the moment and used the wrong lever arm
defect_14.now: DG 1 Eq. 3.4.5: Mpl = Tu*x/B with NO 1/2; Eq. 3.4.6: x = f - d/2 + tf/2
defect_14.direction: UNCONSERVATIVE — the spurious /2 made tp exactly 1/sqrt(2) = 0.707 of DG 1's, 29% low
defect_14.api_change: BasePlateGeometry gained an optional tf. When omitted the module falls back to x = f - d/2 and WARNS, because dropping tf/2 shortens the lever and is unconservative.
defect_14.note: in Case C the bearing interface governs (38.9 mm vs 14.3 mm), so this error did not bite there — but it would on a geometry where the tension side controls

residual_limitations: these equations were read off scanned pages. The transcription risk now sits on THIS side of the comparison, not the tool's. Anyone re-checking should read Sects. 3.1.2, 3.3 and 3.4 directly rather than trusting this fixture.
DG 1 has no explicit uplift-plus-moment case. The defect #9b fix extends Eq. 3.4.3 with Pr carried through signed — a direct extension, but not something DG 1 states.
the small-moment case (e <= e_crit, DG 1 Sect. 3.3) was read but not separately exercised against a worked example.
no DG 1 worked example was run end to end. The check is equation-by-equation, which catches a wrong formula but not a wrong procedure.
